newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- MARCH 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- MARCH 13.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
KATHIMERINI

--The total deregulation of forex accounts within the month is being planned by the Bank of Greece, sources say. The same sources say the development is due to the exchange policies being followed and the confidence created by the hard drachma.

--Deputy Finance Minister George Drys told representatives of the Athens Chamber of Commerce yesterday that the TAXIS computer program will be completed by 1998 and will provide the basis for the abolition of the "objective criteria system".

--The labour market looks to be in good shape for the next two years, according to the national economy ministry. Employment is expected to increase by 0.3 this year and 0.4 in 1998, with unemployment falling from 10.0 percent this year to 9.4 percent in 1998.
IMERISIA

--The government will stick by its targets and incomes policy and will not give in to any pressure, Prime Minister Costas Simitis said last night, in his first television interview since the election.
--Greece' banking system is similar to a "petrified forest", National Bank of Greece Governor Theodoros Karatzas said yesterday, stressing the need for reforms and modernisation.
--The sudden fall in prices at the Athens Stock Exchange yesterday surprised experts, who said it was inexplicable given the course of macroeconomic indicators.
KERDOS

--Simitis promised a quick end to the issue of the name of the Former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia and said that Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos and Deputy Yiannos Kranidiotis will be in Tirana tomorrow as part of joint efforts to resolve the Albanian crisis peacefully.

--The creation of conditions for the participation of private capital in state-run banks and the strengthening of the National and Commercial bank Groups are the basic axes of government policy in the banking sector.

--A GDP growth rate this year of 3.3 percent means that Greece will, for the second year in a row, truly converge with the European Union, National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou said yesterday.
EXPRESS

--Prime Minister Costas Simitis once again warned there was no point in pushing for hand-outs, in his interview last night, saying the goal of equal participation in European Economic and Monetary Union was more important.
--Papandoniou stressed to the Hellenic Banking Association yesterday that a reduction of the difference in lending and deposit interest rates is imperative.
--Papandoniou will chair meetings today on raising revenues for the state through exploitation of the state's property holdings.
NAFTEMBORIKI
--The National Bank is rescheduling debts worth 200 billion drachmas. Sources say the development will help up to 13,000 debtors.
--A further five insurance companies are facing closure by the development ministry. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
